# **CFTC and ETF Report** _A weekly update of futures and exchange traded fund activity._ - Risk-on was the order of the week after Eurozone officials reached agreement on a second bailout package for Greece. Despite several false dawns in recent months, the latest deal was sufficiently robust to assuage markets’ fears over the possibility of a Greek default, currency exit and all that these would entail. Investors voted with their feet, sending the Euro above $1.34 for the first time since early December and propelling global equities indices to new highs for the year. An additional consequence of improved risk sentiment was a weaker USD, which assisted a rall across the precious complex. • Platinum was last week’s star performer. After repeatedly testing $1,650 on February 20th, it broke through and rallied virtually unimpeded for the next three days, peaking above $1,730 on the 23rd. Having languished for much of the year, platinum’s catch-up was not wholly unexpected, although the velocity of its recovery took some by surprise. Fears over supply disruptions caused by strikes at South African mines initially failed to provide much support, but the headlines eventually started to push prices higher as rumours circulated that the disorder could translate to a supply squeeze of many tens of thousands of ounces. The gold-platinum spread narrowed to almost $50 at one point, and spread trading certainly appeared to be a contributing factor to platinum’s outperformance. • Net long speculative positions in gold on Comex rebounded strongly in the week ending February 21st. The move through $1,750 had the market eyeing an approach to $1,800 and beyond; having trimmed long positions by 1.3 million ounces in the previous week, investors piled enthusiastically back into gold, adding more than 2.3 million ounces. The move to $1,800 has not yet transpired, however, so we would expect to see evidence that this bullishness has cooled somewhat in next week’s figures. #### **David Jollie** **david.jollie@mitprecious.com Tel: +44 20 7489 6767** **28 February 2012** #### **New York:** 200 Park Avenue, New York, NY 10166 0130 Tel: +1 212 878 4122 #### **London:** 4th Floor, St Martins Court, 10 Paternoster Row, London EC4M 7BB Tel: +44 20 7489 6767 #### **Hong Kong:** Suite 1306, Two Exchange Square, 8 Connaught Place, Central, Hong Kong Tel: +852 2899 2026 #### **Tokyo:** 2-1 Ohtemachi 1-Chome, Chiyoda-Ku, Tokyo 100 Tel: +81 33 285 3407 #### **Singapore:** 80 Robinson Road, #15-02, Singapore, 068898 Tel: +65 6372 8050 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** **28 February 2012** ## **Gold CFTC data to 21 February 2012; ETF data to 24 February 2012.** |**Exchang**|**e (COMEX a**

The yellow metal peaked above $1,780 on February 23rd, up $70 on the week. Risk-on was the order of the week after Eurozone officials reached agreement on a second bailout package for Greece. Despite several false dawns in recent months, the latest deal was sufficiently robust to assuage markets’ fears over the possibility of a Greek default, currency exit and all that these would entail. Investors voted with their feet, sending the Euro above $1.34 for the first time since early December and propelling global equities indices to new highs for the year. An additional consequence of improved risk sentiment was a weaker USD, which assisted gold’s rally. - Net long speculative positions on Comex rebounded strongly in the week ending February 21st. The move through $1,750 had the market eyeing an approach to $1,800 and beyond; having trimmed long positions by 1.3 million ounces in the previous week, investors piled enthusiastically back into gold, adding more than 2.3 million ounces. The move to $1,800 has not yet transpired, however, so we would expect to see evidence that this bullishness has cooled somewhat in next week’s figures. - An appetite for gold was evident also in ETF flows last week. Having added just 38,000 ounces during the previous week, the range of gold ETFs that we monitor most closely had added between them more than 150,000 ounces. Two of the largest—SPDR and iShares Gold— accounted for almost all of this total. - The silver price took off last week: another break above $34.00 on February 21st followed by hold above here the following day made for a bullish technical picture and helped unleash some pentup buying interest. Another big move the next day took out the 200-day moving average and silver closed above $35.00 for the first time since November. The technical triple-jump was completed when a significant upside trendline was reached at the end of the week; at the time of writing silver has broken through this as well and is trading above $36.00. While silver certainly benefitted from the weaker US Dollar and the broader riskrally seen last week, the succession of technical buy-signs ensured that its gains in percentage te

rms comfortably outstripped those of the other precious metals. 375 50 Silver price, $/oz

- Since the major price action in silver came after the last date for which this report has CFTC data, it is unsurprising that these figures look relatively unremarkable. Net speculative long positions increase by 10.5 million ounces—an almost identical increase to the previous week (10.3 million ounces). - Last week saw modest ETF buying: 2.5 million ounces were added to holdings, partially reversing the previous week’s 3.9 million ounce liquidation. Again, the largest silver ETF (iShares) was responsible for almost all of the buying. Like in gold, strong buying in US-based funds was offset by selling from European funds. 3 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** **28 February 2012** ## **Platinum CFTC data to 21 February 2012; ETF data to 24 February 2012.** ## **Exchange (Nymex and TOCOM) and ETF Platinum Investment (oz)** |**Date**|**Nymex**

- Platinum was last week’s star performer. After repeatedly testing $1,650 on February 20th, it broke through and rallied virtually unimpeded for the next three days, peaking above $1,730

on the 23rd. Having languished for much of the year, platinum’s catch-up was not wholly unexpected, although the velocity of its recovery took some by surprise. Fears over supply disruptions caused by strikes at South African mines initially failed to provide much support, but the headlines eventually started to push prices higher as rumours circulated that the disorder could translate to a supply squeeze of many tens of thousands of ounces. The gold-platinum spread narrowed to almost $50 at one point, and spread trading certainly appeared to be a contributing factor to platinum’s outperformance. - Like silver, platinum’s move higher began on February 21st and so will not necessarily be reflected in the futures and options exchange data. Action here was relatively muted: net long speculative positions increased by 45,000 ounces—less than half the previous week’s increase of 112,000 ounces. The lack of exchange interest in platinum during this period reflects the choppy, unconvincing price action that preceded the rally. - ETF flows in platinum were also unremarkable. Clearly, these were not among the buyers that drove platinum higher initially.
